POL-GEN-OCR.rule: A value the reader had to repair (a letter read as a digit, a word one character off) is shown with the repair. If a Pass or Fail would rest on it, the line is Could Not Evaluate until the sheet is checked.

POL-GEN-UNCOVERED.title: No rule, no verdict
POL-GEN-UNCOVERED.rule: A situation no policy covers is Could Not Evaluate with 'needs a policy decision'.

POL-H-INTERPRETATION.title: Brief rules may support a verdict, disclosed
POL-H-INTERPRETATION.rule: A mapping that rests on the challenge brief rather than code text (R-3 read as row R, because IBC 310 is not provided) may support a Pass or Fail, but the finding names it as an interpretation. The limit value itself always comes from code text.

POL-H-FOOTNOTES.title: Footnotes are cited; pointed-to documents are listed, not assumed
POL-H-FOOTNOTES.rule: Every footnote on the looked-up cell is quoted in the finding. Where a footnote points to a document we don't have (Chapters 4 and 5 exceptions, IBC 903.2.8), the finding lists it as not provided. It does not block the verdict: an exception has to be claimed by the applicant, and the finding says which claims the code analysis makes.

POL-H-NS-NEW.title: NS limits are for existing buildings
POL-H-NS-NEW.rule: If the building resolves to the NS sub-row and the code analysis describes new work, the NS limit is not a basis for a verdict (footnote d): Could Not Evaluate, with the sprinkler status to be confirmed.

POL-H-STATED-HEIGHT.title: The stated height is used as submitted
POL-H-STATED-HEIGHT.rule: The building height is the architect's figure. The tool compares it with the table; it cannot check the measurement (grade plane and roof heights are on sheets not provided), and says so.

POL-H-ARCHITECT.title: The architect's allowable height is checked, not trusted
POL-H-ARCHITECT.rule: If the code analysis states an allowable height that differs from the looked-up cell, the finding flags it and lists the cells in the same row and column that hold the architect's figure, as a likely explanation. The verdict uses the looked-up cell.

POL-H-SPRINKLER-COVERAGE.title: Sprinkler coverage must be 'throughout'
POL-H-SPRINKLER-COVERAGE.rule: S, S13R and S13D are for buildings 'equipped throughout'. Wording that says partial coverage resolves to no sub-row (Could Not Evaluate). Wording that names a standard but not 'throughout' is resolved and flagged.

POL-E-SCOPE.title: Which buildings and floors 1030 covers
POL-E-SCOPE.rule: R-3 and R-4: applies. R-2: Could Not Evaluate unless the exits per story are known. Other groups: Not Applicable. Sleeping rooms must be below the fourth story above grade plane; the story comes from the code analysis room numbering (floor n read as story n above grade plane), else from the number of stories. Unknown story: Could Not Evaluate.

POL-E-SLEEPING.title: What counts as a sleeping room
POL-E-SLEEPING.rule: Room names with a bedroom word (BEDROOM, BED, BDRM, GUEST BED ...) are sleeping rooms, including a word one character from BEDROOM (OCR), which is flagged. Dens, offices, lofts and unrecognised names are ambiguous: not treated as sleeping rooms, but listed for the plan checker to confirm.

POL-E-ROOM-KEY.title: Room identity
POL-E-ROOM-KEY.rule: Windows belong to the same room when their location has the same room number ('BEDROM 12' and 'BEDROOM 12'); without a number, when the names match. Different spellings under one number are flagged.

POL-E-NOT-SLEEPING.title: Windows outside sleeping rooms
POL-E-NOT-SLEEPING.rule: Windows in rooms that are not sleeping rooms are Not Applicable. A window in such a room that is marked egress is noted.

POL-E-NOT-DESIGNATED.title: Sleeping-room windows not marked egress
POL-E-NOT-DESIGNATED.rule: Not Applicable as a window finding: 1030 needs one complying opening per sleeping room, not every window. They are still considered in the room finding.

POL-E-NOMINAL-UPPER.title: Nominal size is an upper bound
POL-E-NOMINAL-UPPER.rule: The net clear opening (area, width and height) is always smaller than the nominal size. A nominal value at or below a minimum proves a Fail; a nominal value above it proves nothing.

POL-E-NO-FRAME-ASSUMPTION.title: No frame-deduction assumption (decision 2)
POL-E-NO-FRAME-ASSUMPTION.rule: The tool assumes no frame size, so nominal size never proves a Pass. Without a net clear opening (from the schedule or manufacturer data) a minimum is Could Not Evaluate, with the nominal upper bound shown.

POL-E-SILL-LOWER.title: A derived sill is a lower bound
POL-E-SILL-LOWER.rule: Sill = head height - nominal height (head height is floor to top of window). The bottom of the clear opening is at or above that frame sill. A frame sill above 44 in proves a Fail; at or below 44 in it proves nothing, because the bottom frame depth is unknown. A scheduled sill height is treated the same way unless the column says it is to the clear opening.

POL-E-GRADE-FLOOR.title: Grade-floor limit (decision 4)
POL-E-GRADE-FLOOR.rule: Whether an opening is a grade-floor opening needs the finished ground level, which these sheets don't give. The area is decided only when the 5.0 and 5.7 sq ft limits give the same result.

POL-E-FIXED.title: A fixed window is not an escape opening
POL-E-FIXED.rule: A window scheduled as fixed does not open, so it can't be operated from inside and has no net clear opening by normal operation: Fail.

POL-E-PARTIAL-OPENING.title: Single hung and slider bounds are notes only (decision 5)
POL-E-PARTIAL-OPENING.rule: A single hung opens only its bottom sash and a slider about half its width. The tool shows the half-size figure as a labelled note, never as proof of a Fail, because panel splits vary (a three-panel slider opens two thirds; sashes can be unequal).

POL-E-OPERATION-UNKNOWN.title: Unrecognised window type
POL-E-OPERATION-UNKNOWN.rule: If the operation isn't recognised, whether and how the window opens is Could Not Evaluate.

POL-E-UNSEEN.title: Requirements no schedule shows
POL-E-UNSEEN.rule: Operation without keys or tools, releasable screens and opening onto a public way, yard or court are each a Could Not Evaluate line on every egress window, naming the document that would settle it. They never cause a Fail; they do keep a window from a Pass.

POL-E-ROOM-ROLLUP.title: Room verdict (decision 3)
POL-E-ROOM-ROLLUP.rule: A sleeping room Passes if a designated egress window Passes, and is Could Not Evaluate if one is Could Not Evaluate. If none is designated, or every designated one Fails, the room's other windows are evaluated as candidates: if any could comply the room is Could Not Evaluate, flagged 'no complying opening designated'; if none could, the room Fails.

POL-E-EXCEPTION-2.title: Exit-door exception is not assumed
POL-E-EXCEPTION-2.rule: A room Fail says 'unless Exception 2 applies (an exit door to a public way)'. The floor plans would settle it; the tool does not assume a door it can't see.

POL-E-NO-EGRESS-COLUMN.title: Schedule without an egress column
POL-E-NO-EGRESS-COLUMN.rule: If the schedule has no egress column, no window is designated. Every sleeping room is then decided by POL-E-ROOM-ROLLUP from its windows as candidates, and the missing column is reported.
